messages:
incidents-bot: PAGER: v-hosted-api - error rate spike > 5% in us-west-1, paging oncall (sev=P1). See /alerts/1798123456 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Paging @sara (oncall) and @mike (backup) for SEV-1

sara: saw the alert, looking. Grafana shows DNS lookup latencies spiking from 20ms -> 800ms and TLS handshakes failing with timeouts. 5xxs from edge gateways. Starting investigation.

mike: confirming — Cloudflare edge metrics show increased 502/524 across multiple POPs in us-west and us-east. Also seeing a sharp rise in SYN_RETRANSMIT at our edge proxies.

dmitri: can you paste the flow? I have phone with Cloudflare on standby but want data to give them.

sara: pasted logs: ```
2026-03-15T10:24:12Z api-gw-03 us-west-1 GET /v1/complete 524 cf_edge:tls_handshake_timeout dns:lookup=820ms 
2026-03-15T10:24:13Z api-gw-02 us-west-1 POST /v1/chat 502 upstream:connect_timeout dns:lookup=650ms
```

emily: Datadog shows our resolvers (internal -> 1.1.1.1) adding +600ms per query, and some NXDOMAIN spikes. Could be Cloudflare authoritative DNS difficulties.

mike: Cloudflare status: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/abc123 - they report degraded performance in some regions for DNS and edge routing.

incidents-bot: NOTE: customer impact likely. Start customer-impact assessment. 

tess: starting C-level impact call mock template. Which customers hit? running quick query...

sara: query: number of active requests returning 5xx in last 10m by account -> ```SELECT account_id, count(*) FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 AND ts > now() - 10m GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20;``` 

mike: top 3 affected are: account_omega (heavy use, real-time chat), account_fjord (low-volume but strict latency SLAs), account_alpha (embeddings batch jobs).

dmitri: mitigation options: (1) Increase retries with exponential backoff in our edge proxies for DNS/TLS stalls (short-term) (2) Shift traffic for affected customers to alternate regions where CF POPs are healthy (3) Temporarily switch DNS resolvers to upstream vendor 8.8.8.8 for affected nodes (risk: cache cold) (4) If Cloudflare offers emergency BGP steering, request immediate evacuation for affected prefixes.

sara: doing 1+2 now. Rolling a hotspot config change to increase connection retries to 3 and DNS query timeout to 2s for west nodes. Also running a traffic-steering rule to prefer us-west-2 over us-west-1 for customer_omega.

mike: preflight check: can you post the rollout command?

sara: ```
# roll hotspot config to increased dns/tls retries
./adminctl rollout --env=prod --scope=us-west --config=retries:dns=3,tls=3,dns_timeout=2000 --reason="cf dns spike"
```

incidents-bot: DEPLOY STARTED by sara (rollout id r-1798123456-1)

emily: note: observability ingestion to Datadog is delayed ~2-5m; metrics may lag during mitigation. Use raw logs from s3 for immediate evidence.

mike: traffic-steer rule applied for account_omega -> now routing to us-west-2. Watching latency.

~5m later~

sara: initial results: retries reduced user-visible 5xxs for most flows, account_omega error rate down from 18% -> 4% after steering and retries. Some customers still intermittent.

dmitri: reach out to Cloudflare on emergency channel: "we're seeing authoritative DNS resolution latency and TLS handshake timeouts from multiple POPs; providing logs + trace ids". Assigning to me.

mike: i'll open a support ticket and CC account rep. Contact: cf-incident@cloudflare-support.example (we have direct line).

dmitri: sent packet captures and timeline. Cloudflare responded: "Investigating DNS resolver backbone causing elevated latencies; mitigating caches and rerouting." ETA unknown.

tess: preparing customer comms. Draft: "We are investigating an external DNS/edge provider incident affecting API reachability for some customers; we've applied temporary routing and retries to reduce impact. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes."

incidents-bot: REMINDER: oncall handoff scheduled in 25m. Current oncall sara -> next oncall mike. Please acknowledge handoff in thread.

sara: acknowledged. Handoff notes: CF DNS spike causing TLS timeouts; mitigations applied: retries increased, traffic-steer to alternate regions, monitoring dashboards pinned; Cloudflare engaged and providing updates. Logs saved to s3://redwood-incidents/1798123456/ for postmortem.

mike: taking over. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate with Cloudflare. If they request BGP evacuation, we'll prep comms and runbook.

emily: started a short-lived synthetic run to validate end-to-end: results show 95th latency improved from 1.2s -> 360ms after steering.

dmitri: Cloudflare posted a mitigation: "Rolling reroutes for affected POPs; expected improvement in next 10-20m."

~20m later~

sara: update from mike: all major accounts recovered to acceptable error rates (<1%). Cloudflare reports incident moving to resolved state for affected DNS backbone.

tess: updating status page and sending customer notification draft to legal for approval.

mike: follow-ups: postmortem items - (1) add fallback resolver chain earlier in our resolver policy (2) automated region-steering when DNS latency > threshold (3) runbook refinement for Cloudflare emergency contact and BGP playbook (4) add more granular per-account retries/traffic steering.

incidents-bot: SEV-1 CLOSED (duration ~43m) - summary: External Cloudflare DNS/edge degradation caused DNS lookup/TLS handshake timeouts in multiple POPs; mitigations (retries, traffic steer) reduced customer impact while provider mitigated. Postmortem assigned to dmitri.

dmitri: will draft timeline and coordinate postmortem, assigning action items. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

mike: filing incident ticket and linking logs: https://redwood-issues.internal/INC-2026-1798123456

emily: adding runbook tasks to eng-sre backlog.

sara: closing channel for now, will reopen if Cloudflare re-escalates.

incidents-bot: This thread will be archived in 7 days.
